You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1.  
  
You need to deploy a Microsoft Purview insider risk management solution that generates an alert when users share sensitive information from Site1 with external recipients.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

options.text: Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy.

questions.explanation:
Insider Risk Management policies establish the users, risk indicators, and priority content—such as a specific SharePoint site and sensitive information types—that are evaluated to generate alerts. The SharePoint indicator for sharing files with people outside the organization must also be enabled, because Insider Risk Management global indicators are disabled by default.

**Learn more:** [Configure policy indicators in Insider Risk Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-settings-policy-indicators) · [Create and manage Insider Risk Management policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-policies)

You deploy Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management for AI (DSPM for AI).  
  
You need to modify the default policies created during the deployment.  
  
Which two Microsoft Purview solutions should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

questions.explanation:

DSPM for AI supplies a Policies page to navigate to the appropriate solution, but policy editing occurs in those underlying solutions. You need to enable Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) for Device1.  
  
What should you do first in the Microsoft Purview portal?

options.text: Enable Microsoft Priva Privacy Risk Management.
Create a Microsoft Purview Information Barriers (IBs) segment.

questions.explanation:

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 tenant that uses Microsoft Teams and includes two users named User1 and User2.  
  
You create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that applies to the Teams chat and channel messages location for User1 and User2.  
  
Which Teams entities will receive DLP protection?

options.text: 1:1/n chats, general channels, and private channels

questions.explanation:
For a Microsoft Purview DLP policy scoped to individual user accounts, protection applies to Teams 1:1 and group chats and to private-channel messages. Standard channels, including a team’s General channel, are not protected by that individual-user scope.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data loss prevention and Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/purview/dlp-microsoft-teams)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 tenant that uses Microsoft Teams and includes two users named User1 and User2.  
  
You create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that applies to the Teams chat and channel messages location for User1 and User2.  
  
Which Teams entities will receive DLP protection?

options.text: Duplicate all the settings from Sublabel1 to Label1.
Delete the policy of Label1 and publish Sublabel1.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft 365 group applies the protection settings configured on the sensitivity label assigned to that container. Sublabels are separate labels and do not cause their settings to be applied through the parent label. Because Label1 is the default label for Group1, configuring Label1 with the same settings as Sublabel1 ensures those settings apply by default.

**Learn more:** [Learn about sensitivity labels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels) · [Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
You need to make sure that you receive an alert when a user uploads a document to a third-party cloud storage service.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps activity policies monitor specified user activities in connected cloud applications and generate alerts for matching activity events. A document upload to a third-party cloud storage service is such an activity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create activity policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/user-activity-policies)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft 365 Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) settings, add a folder path to the file path exclusions.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Endpoint DLP file path exclusions remove files in the specified location from DLP monitoring, alerting, and policy enforcement. They do not block a particular locally installed application from accessing sensitive documents; they instead exempt the folder’s files from protection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure endpoint DLP settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-configure-endpoint-settings)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an app discovery policy in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps app discovery policies are for identifying and alerting on discovered cloud applications, not for restricting a local executable’s access according to a document’s sensitive-content status. Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP provides restricted-app controls for sensitive items on onboarded Windows 11 devices, allowing a specified application to be blocked from sensitive documents without blocking its access to other documents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud discovery policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/policies-cloud-discovery) · [Learn about Endpoint data loss prevention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about)

questions.domain: Implement data loss prevention and retention
questions.question:
Solution: In Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, mark the application as **Unsanctioned**.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Unsanctioned designation in Defender for Cloud Apps blocks access to a cloud application's domains; it does not prevent a locally installed executable from opening sensitive documents. Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP can block a listed restricted app when it attempts to access a DLP-protected file, while leaving its access to other documents unaffected.\
\
**Learn more:** [Govern discovered apps using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/mde-govern) · [Configure endpoint DLP settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-configure-endpoint-settings)

You create a label that encrypts email data.  
  
Users report that they cannot use the label in Outlook on the web to protect the email messages they send.  
  
You need to make sure that users can use the new label to protect their email.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Wait six hours and ask the users to try again.
Create a new sensitive information type.
Modify the priority order of label policies.

questions.explanation:
Sensitivity labels are not available for users to select in Outlook until they are included in a label policy published to those users. Publishing makes the label visible in supported apps and applies its configured encryption protection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and publish sensitivity labels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/create-sensitivity-labels)

questions.question:
You create a label that encrypts email data.  
  
Users report that they cannot use the label in Outlook on the web to protect the email messages they send.  
  
You need to make sure that users can use the new label to protect their email.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: a remote domain in Microsoft Exchange

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Advanced Message Encryption sets external-recipient message expiration in a custom branding template, using `New-OMEConfiguration -ExternalMailExpiryInDays 7`. A mail flow rule is subsequently used to apply that template to encrypted messages.

**Learn more:** [Set an expiration date for email encrypted by Microsoft Purview Advanced Message Encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ome-advanced-expiration) · [Add your brand to encrypted messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/add-your-organization-brand-to-encrypted-messages)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to create static retention policies for the following locations:  
  
- Teams chats  
- Exchange email  
- SharePoint sites  
- Microsoft 365 Groups  
- Teams channel messages  
  
What is the minimum number of retention policies needed?
questions.explanation:
For static retention policies, selecting a Teams location automatically excludes the non-Teams locations. Teams chats and Teams channel messages can be selected together in one policy, while Exchange email, SharePoint sites, and Microsoft 365 Groups can be combined in a second policy. Therefore, the minimum is two policies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and configure a retention policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/create-retention-policies)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to review a usage report for Microsoft 365 Copilot.  
  
Where should you review the report?

options.text: Information Protection in the Microsoft Purview portal
DSPM for AI in the Microsoft Purview portal

questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reporting is available in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Reports > Usage. It provides adoption, retention, engagement, and app-use metrics for Microsoft 365 Copilot.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-365-copilot-usage?view=o365-worldwide) · [Microsoft 365 Copilot reporting options for admins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/microsoft-365-copilot-reports-for-admins)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing two users named User1 and Admin1. Admin1 manages the subscription’s audit retention policies.  
  
You need to ensure that User1’s audit logs are retained for 10 years.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Assign a Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) add-on license to Admin1.
Assign a 10-year audit log retention add-on license to Admin1.
Assign a Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) add-on license to User1.
Assign a 10-year audit log retention add-on license to User1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 E5 includes Audit (Premium), but 10-year audit retention requires a separate 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on for the user who generates the audit records. Assigning that add-on to User1 satisfies the licensing prerequisite before a 10-year audit retention policy can retain User1’s records.

**Learn more:** [Learn about auditing solutions in Microsoft Purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-solutions-overview) · [Manage audit log retention policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-retention-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning a data loss prevention (DLP) solution that applies to Windows Client computers.  
  
You need to ensure that when users try to copy a file containing sensitive information to a USB storage device, these requirements are satisfied:  
  
- If users are members of a group named Group1, they must be permitted to copy the file and an event must be written to the audit log.  
- All other users must be prevented from copying the file.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: one DLP policy that contains one DLP rule
one DLP policy that contains two DLP rules
two DLP policies that each contains one DLP rule

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP policies that include the Devices location can be scoped by users and groups, and a rule can audit or block copying sensitive files to removable USB devices. Separate policy scopes are needed to apply an audit-only action to Group1 and a block action to all other users.

**Learn more:** [Data Loss Prevention policy reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-policy-reference) · [Create and deploy a data loss prevention policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-deploy-policy)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784211861072-uukifec7.png)  
  
How many alerts will be added to the Microsoft Purview portal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 E5 has a one-minute alert-aggregation interval. Subsequent events matching the same alert policy within one minute of the first event are added to that alert rather than generating another. Policy1 therefore produces three alerts, while Policy2 produces one, for a total of four alerts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Alert policies in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/alert-policies)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
You have a database that stores customer details. Every customer has a unique 13-digit identifier made up of a fixed pattern of numbers and letters.  
  
You need to implement a data loss prevention (DLP) solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Email messages containing one customer identifier can be sent outside your company.  
- Email messages containing two or more customer identifiers must be approved by the company's data privacy team.  
  
Which two components should be included in the solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A custom sensitive information type can detect the customer identifier by its fixed alphanumeric pattern. An Exchange Online mail flow rule can apply when a message contains that sensitive information type at least twice and is addressed externally, then forward the message to the data privacy team for approval before delivery.

**Learn more:** [Create custom sensitive information types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-create-a-custom-sensitive-information-type) · [Mail flow rule conditions and exceptions in Exchange Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/mail-flow-rules/conditions-and-exceptions)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing a sensitivity label named Sensitivity1.  
  
You plan to create an auto-labeling policy that applies Sensitivity1 to Microsoft Exchange Online mailboxes.  
  
On February 1, you create the auto-labeling policy and enable simulation mode using the default settings. The policy is not modified while in simulation mode.  
  
When will the policy first be turned on?
questions.explanation:
Simulation mode does not itself enable an auto-labeling policy for production use. Automatic activation requires an AutoEnableAfter period to be configured; its default value is None. Therefore, an unmodified policy remains in simulation mode until it is manually turned on.\
\

You have a Microsoft 365 tenant with a retention label policy.  
  
You need to configure the policy to meet these requirements:  
  
- Prevent the policy from being disabled or deleted.  
- Ensure that new labels can be added.  
- Prevent labels from being removed.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
A Preservation Lock on a retention label policy prevents the policy from being disabled or deleted. It also permits adding labels while preventing existing labels from being removed, so policy protection can be increased but not reduced.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Preservation Lock to restrict changes to retention policies and retention label policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention-preservation-lock)

Microsoft 365 Copilot requires the Copy (EXTRACT) usage right to access and summarize content protected by a sensitivity label. Owner and Editor permissions include that right, whereas Restricted Editor and Viewer permissions do not.

You need to identify every change made to retention labels over the past 30 days.  
  
What should you use in the Microsoft Purview portal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Activity explorer provides a historical view of labeled-content activities sourced from Microsoft 365 audit logs. It includes retention-label changes and reports up to 30 days of data, allowing retention-label activity to be filtered by date and activity type.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with Activity explorer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/data-classification-activity-explorer) · [Learn about retention policies and retention labels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing a data loss prevention (DLP) policy named DLP1. DLP1 includes the DLP rules shown in the table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784214585937-oazauqm7.png)  
  
You need to ensure that, when a document matches every rule, users see Tip 2.  
  
What should you change?

options.text: the priority setting of Rule2 to 0
the priority setting of Rule2 to 2
the priority setting of Rule3 and Rule4 to 0
the if there’s a match for this rule, stop processing additional DLP policies and rules setting for Rule3 to Enabled

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview DLP rules are processed from highest to lowest priority, with priority 0 being highest. When multiple matching rules have the same notification action, the policy tip from the highest-priority rule is shown. Assigning Rule2 priority 0 makes Rule2 the highest-priority matching rule, so users see Tip 2.

**Learn more:** [Data Loss Prevention policy reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-policy-reference) · [Set-DlpComplianceRule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-dlpcompliancerule?view=exchange-ps)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 tenant.  
  
You create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy.  
  
You need to make sure the policy protects documents in Microsoft Teams chat sessions.  
  
Which location should you enable in the policy?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview DLP protects the actual content of Microsoft Teams chats and channel messages through the **Teams chat and channel messages** location. SharePoint and OneDrive locations apply to files stored in those services, whereas the Teams location is needed for chat-message protection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data loss prevention and Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-microsoft-teams) · [Data Loss Prevention policy reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-policy-reference)

Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to monitor Microsoft 365 Copilot user prompts and responses for content matched by the Protected Materials trainable classifier.  
  
Which policy type should you create?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance policies monitor Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions and can apply Microsoft-provided trainable classifiers. The Protected material classifier detects known text that may be protected by copyright or branding laws in generative AI responses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure a Communication Compliance policy to detect generative AI interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/communication-compliance-copilot) · [Trainable classifier definitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/trainable-classifiers-definitions)

Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to monitor Microsoft 365 Copilot user prompts and responses for content matched by the Protected Materials trainable classifier.  
  
Which policy type should you create?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview does not support Preservation Lock for retention policies that use adaptive policy scopes. A retention policy with a static scope, including one targeting Microsoft 365 groups, can support Preservation Lock.

**Learn more:** [Use Preservation Lock to restrict changes to retention policies and retention label policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention-preservation-lock)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a retention label with a retention period of seven years.  
  
You need to ensure that documents that contain a credit card number are retained for seven years. Other documents must not be retained.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: a retention label policy of type auto-apply
a retention label policy of type publish
a retention policy that deletes files automatically
a retention policy that retains files automatically

questions.explanation:
An auto-apply retention label policy can apply a retention label when content contains a specified sensitive information type, such as a credit card number. Applying the seven-year label only to matching documents meets the retention requirement without retaining other documents.

**Learn more:** [Automatically apply a retention label to retain or delete content](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/apply-retention-labels-automatically) · [Learn about retention policies and retention labels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 tenant with a retention label named Label1.  
  
You must create an auto-labeling policy that applies Label1.  
  
To which location can Label1 be applied?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview auto-apply retention label policies can target OneDrive accounts. Teams chats do not support retention labels and instead require retention policies; Microsoft Entra security groups and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps are not supported auto-labeling locations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Learn about retention policies and retention labels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention)

You plan to create the Microsoft Purview policies shown in the following table.

Which policies can use EDM1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview EDM sensitive information types can be used by Data Loss Prevention and Insider Risk Management policies. Retention policies do not support EDM classifiers as policy conditions.\
\

**Learn more:** [Export Content search results](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/purview/ediscovery-export-search-results)

Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:

Solution: You configure a mail flow rule that matches a sensitive information type.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: Matching a sensitive information type is only a mail-flow rule condition. questions.question:

Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A DLP policy’s selected locations establish the content locations to which its rules apply. Email encryption requires a DLP rule that detects the relevant content and is configured with the **Encrypt email messages** action, which applies only to Exchange content. Selecting Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams locations by itself does not configure such an encryption rule.\
\

Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:

- Exchange Online email  
- SharePoint Online sites

questions.explanation:
EDM primary elements must be detectable through an existing sensitive information type with a defined pattern. The EU Passport Number and All Full Names fields meet that requirement. questions.explanation:

Microsoft 365 Copilot honors the user’s existing permissions and sensitivity-label encryption rights, so content protected for authorized users is not included in responses for users who lack those rights.

You create a communication compliance policy named Policy1 and select **Detect Microsoft Copilot interactions**.  
  
Which two trainable classifiers are automatically added to Policy1? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The Detect Microsoft Copilot interactions template uses the Prompt Shields and Protected material classifiers. Prompt Shields detects adversarial prompt-injection attempts, while Protected material detects known content that may be protected by copyright or branding laws.\

questions.question:
You must enable a user to view data loss prevention (DLP) alerts in the Microsoft Purview portal. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to the user?
questions.explanation:
The Security Reader role provides read-only access to security-related features, including viewing DLP alerts in the Microsoft Purview portal. It does not grant the alert-management or broader administrative permissions provided by Security Operator, Compliance Data Administrator, or Compliance Administrator.\
\

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to enable support for sensitivity labels in Microsoft SharePoint Online.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview is the portal used to enable SharePoint and OneDrive support for sensitivity labels. In Microsoft Purview, go to **Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels** and select **Turn on now** when prompted to enable processing of labeled Office online files.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to create a sensitivity label named Label1. The solution must ensure that users can use Microsoft 365 Copilot to summarize files to which Label1 is applied.  
  
Which permission should you choose for Label1?
questions.explanation:
For Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Microsoft 365 Copilot can return and summarize file content only when the user has the EXTRACT usage right (in addition to VIEW). EXTRACT is the permission that allows Copilot to copy or extract the protected content for summarization.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft 365 Copilot data protection architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/microsoft-365-copilot-architecture-data-protection-auditing) · [Use Microsoft Purview to manage data security and compliance for Microsoft 365 Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-m365-copilot-considerations)

options.text: Run the policy in simulation mode.

questions.explanation:

From Exchange Online PowerShell, run Start-ManagedFolderAssistant.
From Exchange Online PowerShell, run Start-RetentionAutoTagLearning.

questions.explanation:
The Managed Folder Assistant processes Exchange Online mailboxes that have a retention policy, stamps applicable mailbox items with the appropriate retention tags, and applies the configured retention actions. `Start-ManagedFolderAssistant` manually initiates this processing for a specified mailbox instead of waiting for its normal schedule.

**Learn more:** [Retention tags and retention policies in Exchange Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/messaging-records-management/retention-tags-and-policies) · [Start-ManagedFolderAssistant (ExchangePowerShell)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/start-managedfolderassistant?view=exchange-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You have a Microsoft SharePoint Online document library containing Microsoft Word and Excel documents. The documents contain these types of information:  
  
- Credit card numbers  
- Physical addresses in the UK  
- National health service numbers from the UK  
- Sensitive projects containing the following words: Project Tailspin, Project Contoso, and Project Falcon  
  
You have email messages in Microsoft Exchange Online that contain these information types:  
  
- Credit card numbers  
- User sign-in credentials  
- National health service numbers from the UK  
  
You plan to use sensitive information types (SITs) for compliance policies.  
  
What is the minimum number of SITs needed to classify every information type?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview includes built-in SITs for credit card numbers, U.K. physical addresses, U.K. National Health Service numbers, and user login credentials. One custom SIT with a keyword list can detect all three project names. The repeated credit-card and NHS-number data in SharePoint and Exchange use the same SITs, so five SITs are required.

**Learn more:** [Sensitive information type entity definitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-sensitive-information-type-entity-definitions) · [Learn about sensitive information types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing two Microsoft SharePoint Online sites, named Site1 and Site2.  
  
You plan to use policies to meet these requirements:  
  
- Add a **Confidential** watermark to a document when it contains the words **Project1** or **Project2**.  
- Retain a document for seven years when it contains credit card information.  
- Add an **Internal Use Only** watermark to every document stored on Site2.  
- Add a **Confidential** watermark to every document stored on Site1.  
  
You need to recommend the minimum number of sensitive information types required.  
  
How many sensitive information types should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Credit card information can be identified with the built-in Credit Card Number sensitive information type. One custom sensitive information type can contain both Project1 and Project2 keyword patterns, so it detects either term. The requirements that apply a watermark to all documents in a particular SharePoint site are scoped by location rather than by content detection and require no additional sensitive information type.

**Learn more:** [Automatically apply a sensitivity label to Microsoft 365 data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically) · [Automatically apply a retention label to Microsoft 365 items](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/apply-retention-labels-automatically)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft Teams channel named Channel1. Channel1 stores research and development documents.  
  
You plan to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot for the subscription.  
  
You need to prevent the contents of files stored in Channel1 from being included in Copilot-generated answers and displayed to unauthorized users.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) can apply policies to Microsoft 365 Copilot that prevent Copilot from processing files matching policy conditions, including sensitivity labels or sensitive-information types. Content that is prevented from processing is excluded from Copilot response summaries.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about) · [Secure and govern Microsoft 365 Copilot agents — Protect interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/deploymentmodels/depmod-sc-agents-step3)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You are implementing insider risk management.  
  
You need to maximize the historical data collected when an event is triggered.  
  
What is the maximum number of days for which historical data can be collected?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management supports a maximum 90-day lookback period for historical data collection for signals other than Exchange Online. Exchange Online is limited to 10 days, so the overall maximum is 90 days.\
\
**Learn more:** [Limits in Insider Risk Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-limits)

What should you do?

options.text: Assign User1 the Global Reader role.

questions.explanation:

options.text: Enable additional processing of the policies if there is a match for Rule1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview evaluates DLP content in priority order, with priority 0 as the highest priority. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],At a project's conclusion, you upload project documents to a Microsoft SharePoint Online library that contains many files. The following are sample project-document file names:

What should you use to identify the files?
questions.explanation:
Auto-apply retention label policies in Microsoft Purview support three condition types: sensitive information types, keyword/searchable-property queries, and trainable classifiers. Trainable classifiers are machine-learning models trained on example documents to recognize unstructured content by topic or theme, and are not suited to detecting an exact, structured naming convention. A consistent structured pattern like the one described is instead matched reliably using a custom, regex-based sensitive information type, so that is the tool used to identify which files should receive the auto-applied retention label.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing two users named User1 and User2.  
  
On January 1, you create the sensitivity label shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784213915015-jfoewg3t.png)  
  
On January 2, you publish Label1 to User.  
  
On January 3, User1 creates a Microsoft Word document named Doc1 and applies Label1 to it.  
  
On January 4, User2 edits Doc1.  
  
On January 15, you increase Label1's content-expiry period to 28 days.  
  
When does User2's access to Doc1 expire?
questions.explanation:
For a sensitivity label configured with Assign permissions now, access expiry is calculated from the date the label is applied to the content. Changes to administrator-defined encryption settings are applied to existing encrypted items when users authenticate with the encryption service; a user who already opened the item receives the revised settings after the current use license expires. The updated 28-day expiry therefore runs from January 3 through January 31.

**Learn more:** [Apply encryption using sensitivity labels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels)

questions.question:
Solution: You run the `Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -AdminAuditLogEnabled $true -AdminAuditLogCmdlets *Mailbox*` command.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
`Set-AdminAuditLogConfig` with `AdminAuditLogEnabled` and `AdminAuditLogCmdlets` configures auditing of Exchange administrator cmdlet executions. A `*Mailbox*` filter selects administrative cmdlets by name; it does not enable recording of mailbox sign-ins or mailbox-access activity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set-AdminAuditLogConfig (ExchangePowerShell)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-adminauditlogconfig?view=exchange-ps)

questions.question:
Solution: You run the `Set-Mailbox -Identity "User1" -AuditEnabled $true` command.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Setting `AuditEnabled` to `$true` enables mailbox auditing for User1, allowing future mailbox activity by delegates with Full Access to be recorded and searched in Microsoft Purview audit logs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage mailbox auditing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-mailboxes) · [Search the audit log to investigate common support issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-troubleshooting-scenarios)

\

Solution: You execute the `Set-MailboxFolderPermission -Identity "User1" -User [email protected] -AccessRights Owner` command.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
`Set-MailboxFolderPermission` modifies permissions for a specific mailbox folder. The `Owner` access right grants folder-level capabilities, but it does not enable or configure mailbox audit logging for future mailbox sign-ins or delegate access.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set-MailboxFolderPermission (ExchangePowerShell)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-mailboxfolderpermission?view=exchange-ps) · [Manage mailbox auditing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-mailboxes)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You create a new trainable classifier.  
  
You must train the classifier.  
  
Which source can you use to train it?

options.text: an on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server site

questions.explanation:
A custom Microsoft Purview trainable classifier is trained with positive and negative seed examples selected from a SharePoint site, document library, and folder. A Microsoft SharePoint Online site therefore provides a supported training source.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with trainable classifiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/trainable-classifiers-get-started-with)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Purview.  
  
You are assessing the use of custom data assessment scans to identify potential data oversharing in the subscription.  
  
What is the maximum number of items that data assessments support per location?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview data risk assessments, including custom assessments used to identify potential oversharing, support a maximum of 200,000 items per location.\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) policy configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784211871413-md3zp136.png)  
  
From a computer named Computer1, a user is sometimes able to upload files to cloud services and sometimes is not. Other users have the same issue.  
  
What are two possible causes of the issue? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: The unallowed browsers in the Microsoft 365 Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) settings are NOT configured.
There are file path exclusions in the Microsoft 365 Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) settings.
The Access by restricted apps action is set to Audit only.
The Copy to clipboard action is set to Audit only.
The computers are NOT onboarded to Microsoft Purview.

questions.explanation:
Endpoint DLP blocks protected-file uploads only when the relevant browser and cloud-service restrictions can be enforced. Browsers not included in the unallowed-browser configuration can provide a route that is not blocked. In addition, files located in configured file-path exclusions are not monitored or subject to DLP policy enforcement, so their uploads can succeed.

**Learn more:** [Configure endpoint DLP settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-configure-endpoint-settings) · [Data Loss Prevention policy reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-policy-reference)

Each product group in the company must display a distinct product logo in encrypted emails rather than the standard Microsoft 365 logo.  
  
What should you do to create the branding templates?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Advanced Message Encryption creates custom branding templates with the `New-OMEConfiguration` cmdlet. Each template can subsequently be customized with its own logo; mail flow rules can apply the appropriate template to encrypted messages.

**Learn more:** [Add your brand to encrypted messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/add-your-organization-brand-to-encrypted-messages) · [New-OMEConfiguration (ExchangePowerShell)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-omeconfiguration?view=exchange-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant that has opted in to trainable classifiers.  
  
You need to ensure that a user named User1 can create custom trainable classifiers. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview permits users with Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator access to create custom trainable classifiers. Compliance Administrator provides the required compliance-classification capability without granting the broader tenant-wide permissions of Global Administrator; Security Operator does not provide this capability.

**Learn more:** [Get started with trainable classifiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/trainable-classifiers-get-started-with) · [Classifiers overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/data-classification-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
The company conducts annual employee assessments. The assessment results are recorded in a document named `AssessmentTemplate.docx`, created by using a Microsoft Word template. Copies of the employee assessments are sent to employees and their managers.  
  
The assessment copies are stored in mailboxes, Microsoft SharePoint Online sites, and OneDrive folders. A copy of every assessment is also stored in a SharePoint Online folder named `Assessments`.  
  
You need to create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that prevents employee assessments from being emailed to external users. You will use a document fingerprint to identify the assessment documents. The solution must minimize effort.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

Import 100 sample documents from the Assessments folder to a seed folder.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview document fingerprinting creates a sensitive information type from a standard form or template, enabling DLP to detect documents created from that form, including documents with completed content. The fingerprint-based sensitive information type can be used in DLP policies for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive, so fingerprinting `AssessmentTemplate.docx` provides the required coverage with the least setup effort.

What is the minimum number of retention policies needed to achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:

A retention policy can apply the same retention settings to multiple locations, including Exchange mailboxes and public folders, SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, Teams chats, and Teams channel messages. Configuring it to retain content for one year across those locations meets the requirement for all users’ Microsoft 365 data. [Microsoft Learn: Learn about retention policies & labels to retain or delete](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention)\

You need to add a new keyword dictionary. What should you create?

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1. Site1 contains a file named File1.  
  
You have a retention policy named Retention1 with these settings:  
  
- Retain items for a specific period  
  - Retention period: 5 years  
  - At the end of the retention period: Delete items automatically  
  
Retention1 is applied to Site1.  
  
You need to ensure that File1 is automatically deleted after seven years. The solution must **not** affect retention for other files on Site1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Publish and apply a new retention label.
Move File1 to a new folder and configure the access control list (ACL) entries for File1.
Move File1 to a new folder and list the excluded locations for Retention1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview retention policies apply settings at the SharePoint site level, whereas retention labels can be assigned to an individual document. A 7-year retention label that deletes the item at the end of its retention period can therefore target File1 without changing the retention settings for other Site1 files. When deletion settings conflict, a retention label’s delete action takes precedence over a retention policy’s delete action.

**Learn more:** [Learn about retention policies and retention labels to retain or delete](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention) · [Learn about retention for SharePoint and OneDrive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention-policies-sharepoint)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company manufactures parts, each of which has a unique 12-character alphanumeric serial number. Email messages between the company and its customers reference the serial number.  
  
You must ensure that only Microsoft Exchange Online emails that contain the serial numbers are retained for five years.  
  
Which three objects should you create? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview auto-apply retention label policies work by scanning content for conditions such as a custom sensitive information type, then automatically applying a previously created retention label (which defines the five-year retention duration) to matching Exchange Online items; a custom sensitive info type using pattern/regex matching is the correct tool for detecting a well-defined 12-character alphanumeric serial number, and only the auto-labeling policy, the sensitive info type, and the retention label together satisfy the requirement to retain only messages that contain the serial number.

**Learn more:** [Automatically apply a retention label to Microsoft 365 items | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/apply-retention-labels-automatically)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant that uses Microsoft Purview Information Protection.  
  
You create a sensitivity label named Sensitivity1 and configure it to encrypt files and emails.  
  
You publish Sensitivity1.  
  
You discover that users are **not** prompted to apply Sensitivity1 to their files and email.  
  
You need to ensure users must apply Sensitivity1 to their files and email before saving files or sending emails. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Prevent users from removing the label from files and emails.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the protection settings of the sensitivity label policy for Sensitivity1.
Publish Sensitivity1 by creating a label policy.

questions.explanation:
A sensitivity label policy can enforce mandatory labeling by requiring users to apply a label before saving an unlabeled document or sending an unlabeled email. This policy setting ensures content cannot be left without a label and avoids creating an additional auto-labeling policy or republishing the label.

**Learn more:** [Manage sensitivity labels in Office apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/purview/sensitivity-labels-office-apps?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management. The subscription includes a policy named Policy1 that detects potential insider risks from exfiltration activities.  
  
You identify multiple high-severity alerts for Policy1.  
  
When reviewing the alerts, you find that the activities that triggered them have a low-risk score.  
  
You need to ensure that you receive high-severity alerts only for activities with a high-risk score.  
  
What should you modify in Policy1?
questions.explanation:
Policy indicator thresholds control how the daily number of risk events affects risk scores and the associated alert severity. Configuring the indicators so that only higher-volume or higher-impact exfiltration activity receives a high risk-score impact ensures that high-severity alerts correspond to high-risk activity.

**Learn more:** [Configure policy indicators in Insider Risk Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-settings-policy-indicators)

You need to identify the users who uploaded confidential files to external websites. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use in the Microsoft Purview portal?
